sections.title: Setting Up a Contrastive Frame
sections.content: Before reaching the pre-verbal focus slot, a Hungarian sentence can establish one or more contrastive topics—elements that shift the reader's perspective from one person, time, or place to another. Expressions such as 'Ami X-et illeti' (As for X), 'X viszont' (X, on the other hand), and 'ezzel szemben' (in contrast to this) occupy the left periphery of the clause.

sections.title: Topic vs. Focus Together
sections.content: Because contrastive topics sit outside the focus slot, they do NOT trigger preverb-verb inversion by themselves unless another focused element follows them: 'Ákos viszont elmosolyodott' (Ákos, however, smiled—neutral comment) vs. 'Ákos viszont a vendéglőt választotta' (Ákos, however, chose the restaurant—focused object).

sections.title: Contrastive Topic Connectors
rows: As for Ákos, he remained silent.
Pacsirta aggódott, a szülei viszont megkönnyebbültek.
Pacsirta was worried; her parents, on the other hand, felt relieved.
A felszínen gyászoltak; ezzel szemben belül felszabadultak.
On the surface they mourned; in contrast, inside they felt liberated.
Míg otthon suttogtak, a vendéglőben hangosan nevettek.
Whereas at home they whispered, in the restaurant they laughed aloud.

items.spanish: Ami az idős házaspárt illeti, ők még percekig néztek a vonat után.
items.english: As for the elderly couple, they watched the train for several more minutes.

items.spanish: Korábban mindentől visszavonultak; most viszont a városi vendéglőbe tértek be.
items.english: Previously they had withdrawn from everything; now, however, they stepped into the town restaurant.

items.spanish: A levelekben panaszkodtak, ezzel szemben esténként színházba jártak.
items.english: In their letters they complained; in contrast, in the evenings they went to the theatre.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: Notice that 'viszont' is a second-position clitic-like conjunction: it naturally follows the contrasted topic ('Ákos viszont...', 'Most viszont...'), rather than standing as the very first word.
